name: Sandbox — run commands isolated from the real machine
description: Run shell commands and source code (Python, JavaScript, Bash, Ruby…) isolated from the real machine, two ways. (1) Directly on this machine but confined by the operating system: macOS uses Seatbelt, Linux uses bubblewrap, Windows uses AppContainer + Job Object. Code runs, but it cannot write outside the sandbox directory and by default cannot read the rest of the disk either. Read access has three selectable levels: full isolation (only the sandbox and the folders you mount — the default), isolation plus an allowlist of folders declared in settings, or reads not isolated. The network is off by default, and can be opened one port at a time: name the ports the sandbox may serve on (reachable at 127.0.0.1) and the only remote ports it may dial out to, so an app can run and be viewed in a browser without also getting general internet access. Starts instantly, nothing to install. (2) Inside a Docker container with CPU/RAM/process limits, all capabilities dropped and a separate network namespace — a firmer boundary, at the cost of needing a running Docker daemon. The app measures what this machine can actually do rather than assuming: if the docker CLI is on PATH but the daemon is dead, it says so and tells you how to fix it. Each sandbox is its own directory that keeps files and installed packages between runs, with a file browser, an interactive terminal, live CPU/RAM charts and a process list (stop one process or all of them), host folders mountable read-only or read-write, a per-run log recording which isolation was actually applied, and optional activity tracing for testing that records file reads and writes, process launches, and which addresses and hostnames were contacted. Commands always reach the shell through stdin, so quotes in your code survive intact; the child environment is built from scratch, so the daemon's API keys never reach the sandbox. The web UI is in English with Vietnamese available from a language switch.

mcp.name: sandbox-mcp
mcp.description: SenClaw Sandbox MCP: check what isolation this machine supports, run a snippet in a throwaway sandbox, create a long-lived sandbox for multi-step work, run shell commands or snippets inside it, install packages with pip/npm/apt, read/write/list files in the sandbox, change resource limits and the network switch, open specific ports for serving or for outbound connections, change the disk read-isolation level, read and change app defaults, watch CPU/RAM and the running processes, stop one process or all of them, mount and unmount real folders from the machine, turn activity tracing on or off and read the recorded file/process/network events, and review run history with the isolation actually applied.
